prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No rice paddy system emits no methane, so the Main KPI of 150,000,000 hectares of low-methane rice is far from met. The best field practices cut methane by about half: alternate wetting and drying reduced methane by 51.6 percent versus continuous flooding in a 2024 Global Change Biology meta-analysis while raising nitrous oxide by 44 percent (https://katalog.dhi-paris.fr/vufind/Record/NLM381115356/Description), and adoption remains limited. Combined AWD with acid-modified straw biochar cut seasonal methane by 75 to 89 percent in a three-year 2025 study (https://biochartoday.com/news/engineered-biochar-and-awd-cut-rice-methane-emissions-by-up-to-90-while-boosting-yield-by-12-in-3-year-field-study/), and Punjab and Indonesia trials began in 2026. Low-methane varieties remain experimental: SUSIBA2 rice cut methane to about 10 percent of control before flowering in Chinese trials (2015, https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1221487) and a non-GMO line reportedly emitted 70 percent less. Meanwhile a May 2026 Nature Food study found rice-paddy greenhouse emissions nearly doubled over six decades, with Asia 90.2 percent of the total and management able to cut about 10 percent without yield loss (https://carbon-pulse.com/514869/). Honest limit: AWD and biochar are known and published, so tasks that re-measure them are known answers; the open work is near-zero-methane rice systems at farm scale without yield or nitrous-oxide penalties, and each task needs its own basis.
